tob-10787: Cambridge chemist Pattison Muir tells how the dream of turning base metals into gold slowly matured into the science of chemistry. He follows the alchemists’ experiments, their theories of matter, and the gradual discovery of the elements. Written with a scientist’s clarity, the book shows how much modern chemistry owes to its mystical ancestor.
tob-4087: A slim late book of Yeats, holding seven finished poems and one fragment from his closing years. Brief as it is, it shows the old master’s last manner — stark, far-seeing, and haunted by Irish history. The fragment is a moving sign of work cut off by death.
tob-0187: Manly P. Hall’s first book retells the old myth of fire as the sign of the waking soul. He tracks the holy flame through Egypt, Greece, and the Christian mysteries, showing how initiates kept its meaning. Written in his twenty-first year, it set the course for his life’s work on veiled wisdom.
tob-4187: John Burnet’s classic history walks the reader from Thales to the Sophists — the first science-men and thinkers of the West. He shows how the Milesians, Heraclitus, Parmenides, and the atom-men reasoned their way to plain accounts of nature. The book stays the clearest English guide to thought’s birth.
tob-9287: Bühler’s Manu turns the great Hindu doom-book — the rede of ranks, life, and kingship that shaped Indian fellowship. A Sacred Books volume, his Englishing stays the standard Manu. Its dooms on rank and duty ruled Indian life two thousand years. The text is the key to olden India.
cia-0000105887: A February 1965 report on Indonesian army staff proposals to tighten internal security, including surveillance of political opponents. The army's G-1 personnel branch was planning how to watch, control, and neutralize threats as the country's politics grew more dangerous. It is a window into the military mindset months before Indonesia's 1965 crisis.
cia-0000107987: The National Intelligence Bulletin of March 5, 1976 — the daily newspaper of American intelligence, summarizing the world's crises for the president and top officials. Each edition distilled overnight reporting into the essentials a leader needed before breakfast. This surviving issue is a time capsule of what Washington worried about on one Cold War day.
cia-0000108487: An August 1981 document, title deleted, concerning an American missionary murdered in Guatemala. Missionaries working among the poor became targets in a war where both sides saw enemies everywhere. The entry preserves one more casualty of Guatemala's long, brutal conflict — and the censorship that still guards parts of the story.
cia-0000115487: An interagency memorandum, estimated to date from February 1981, on Nicaraguan support for Salvadoran insurgents. The Sandinistas were arming El Salvador's guerrillas, and Washington wanted proof on paper. The memo captures the Reagan administration building its Central America case, agency by agency.
cia-0000117887: A Latin America brief for February 14, 1992 — part of its title deleted — noting Guatemala showing progress. By 1992 the Cold War was over and Guatemala's war was winding down. The brief's guarded optimism reflects a region, and an agency, adjusting to peace.
cia-0000118687: An estimated August 1989 study — part of its title deleted — on Gorbachev's domestic gambles and instability in the USSR. The Soviet leader's reforms were unleashing forces he could not control. The document shows American analysts watching the Soviet experiment wobble, wondering how far the fall would go.
cia-0000119587: An estimated August 1966 document, source deleted, on North Vietnamese guidance suggested to Eastern-bloc countries. Hanoi was lobbying its communist allies for more support in the war. The censored source hides who reported it, but the subject is clear: North Vietnam working the alliance for all it was worth.
cia-0000126887: A January 1968 report on South Vietnamese Vice President Ky's intention to give up his special powers — the truncated title cuts off his reason. Ky, the flamboyant airman-politician, was maneuvering against President Thieu. The document is Saigon intrigue: generals jockeying while the war burned.
cia-0000132287: Situation Report 596: Baghdad believing the ground war had begun — the truncated title hints at more. Perception mattered: what Iraq thought was happening shaped what it did. The document captures the fog of war from the losing side.
cia-0000132587: A September 1960 report: the USSR increasing its attention to Cuba. Moscow's courtship was intensifying — more deals, more visits, more promises. The document tracks the rising temperature: the superpower, leaning in.
cia-0000132687: A 1961 preliminary assessment of the consequences for America of the failed rebellion in Castro's Cuba — the Bay of Pigs, assessed. The disaster's fallout was still spreading. The document is the reckoning: the failure, costed.
cia-0000132787: A 1960 study titled The Cuban Militia. The revolution's armed people, examined. The document is the militia, dissected: the citizens, weaponized.
cia-0000136087: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN providing cargo flight schedules. The supply runs, timetabled. The document is the schedule: the cargo, flown — on time.
cia-0000136187: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN for BRODFROST on a leaflet drop. The paper war, continued. The document is the drop: the leaflets, delivered.
cia-0000136287: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN for LANGEVIN on broadcasts. The airwaves, once more. The document is the standing order: the broadcasts, continued.
cia-0000136887: A 1954 cable to the senior representative at LINCOLN on an individual accepting a proposition — the archive's spelling says porposition — and requesting something, the truncated title cuts off. cia-0000136987: A 1954 cable advising that a reference to Czechoslovakia in the Guatemala situation required something — the truncated title cuts off what. The talking point, flagged. The document is the advice: the reference, handled.
cia-0000139487: A 1954 report on sightings of Caucasian communist personnel in North Korea. The foreigners, spotted. The document is the sighting: the personnel, seen.

un-sc-res-387: Security Council Resolution 387, adopted in 1976. The late-seventies Council at work. The designation and year endure; the act is in the text.

cia-0000135687: A 1960 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents, numbered 0000135687. The brigade's Spanish documents, pre-invasion. The document is the prelude: the papers, early.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d87: President Roosevelt to Prime Minister Churchill, November 2, 1943 — the truncated title cuts off the rest — Document 87. Washington to London. The message is the link: the allies, conferring.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d187: A memorandum by the representatives of the British Chiefs of Staff, November 3 — the truncated title cuts off the year — Document 187. Britain's military minds, on paper. The memo is the military's: the chiefs, represented.

arxiv-2605-08787: Radiologists read CT scans as three-dimensional volumes, yet AI models that answer questions about them often get lost in the depth. Mashrafi Monon and colleagues introduce CT-SpatialVQA, a benchmark that measures whether medical vision-language models truly grasp spatial relationships inside 3D scans. The paper gives the field a shared yardstick for semantic and spatial understanding in volumetric imaging.
arxiv-2605-09087: Fake voices are getting good, and detectors that cry wolf — or miss the wolf — cannot be trusted. Aishwarya Fursule, Shruti Kshirsagar, and Anderson R. Avila propose a systematic framework for diagnosing and mitigating the weaknesses of audio deepfake detection. The 2026 paper is about making voice-forgery detectors worthy of trust.
arxiv-2605-09187: Who did what to whom — semantic roles — is the skeleton of meaning, and models were never explicitly taught it. Carla Griffiths and Mirco Musolesi find emergent semantic role understanding in language models. The 2026 paper asks what grammar AI learns on its own.
arxiv-2605-09587: Biharmonic surfaces generalize minimal surfaces to a fourth-order energy, and one might expect wilder behavior. Shun Maeta proves that rotational biharmonic surfaces in four-dimensional Euclidean space are minimal after all. The 2026 paper is differential geometry with a satisfying punchline.
arxiv-2605-09887: Sparse autoencoders scale in predictable ways; manifold structure predicts the layerwise scaling laws — the geometric wall. Eslam Zaher, Maciej Trzaskowski, Quan Nguyen, and Fred Roosta discover it. The 2026 paper is interpretability research hitting a hard geometric limit head-on today.
plos-pone-0003387: Muscle researchers linked a misplaced enzyme to muscle disease in this 2008 mouse study. The protein nNOSmu normally anchors to the muscle membrane through the dystrophin complex, making nitric oxide where fibers need it. Mice lacking it developed myopathy, a mix of weakness and fiber damage, showing the enzyme is not a bystander but essential for healthy skeletal muscle.
plos-pone-0003487: Neuroscientists restored memory with a vitamin in this 2008 rat study. Animals deprived of vitamin A lost the birth of new neurons in the hippocampus and forgot spatial tasks, but retinoic acid treatment reversed both. The work ties the retinoid signaling pathway directly to adult brain regeneration and the memory it supports.
plos-pone-0003587: Geneticists Wegmann, Dupanloup, and Excoffier found that busy genes splice more creatively in this 2008 paper. Genes expressed across many conditions, a wide expression profile, showed more alternative splicing, the cut-and-paste that multiplies protein variety. The link suggests that how widely a gene is used drives how many forms it takes.
plos-pone-0003687: In 2008, Merlo and Romano found forgetting needs a molecular brake. When a fear memory was extinguished by re-exposure without harm, the transcription factor NF-kB had to be switched off for the forgetting to stick. The result shows memory extinction is an active shutdown, not a passive fade.
plos-pone-0003787: Santi, Pezzicoli, and Bosello characterized a strep enzyme that trains immunity in this 2008 paper. The pullulanase of Group B Streptococcus, a metabolic tool for surviving in the host, triggered antibody responses. The immunogenic enzyme is a candidate piece for future vaccines.
plos-pone-0003887: In 2008, a team measured how much malaria risk runs in families. Studying a Karen population in Thailand, they estimated the heritability of falciparum and vivax malaria. The family-based numbers separate inherited susceptibility from mere shared exposure.
plos-pone-0003987: In 2008, Beaufays, Adam, and Menten-Dedoyart caught a tick disarming immune cells. The tick's saliva protein Ir-LBP grabbed LTB4, a rallying signal for neutrophils. Without their chemical call to arms, neutrophils failed to swarm the bite site. The lipocalin reveals yet another tick trick for feeding long and undisturbed.
plos-pone-0004087: In 2008, Bossi, Gay, and Fouzai studied just who answers the smallpox shot best. Demographic and clinical factors were linked to vaccine response in preimmunized volunteers. France's 2003 biodefense program supplied the study cohort. The predictors help health teams target revaccination wisely today.
plos-pone-0004187: In 2009, a Polish team traced transplant artery clogging. Host smooth muscle cells piled up in transplanted hearts. Inflammation drew the recipient's own cells into the graft. The finding reframes transplant vessel disease biology. Blocking the inflow could save transplanted hearts.
plos-pone-0004287: In 2009, Doxiadis, Heijmans, and Bonhomme unraveled monkey immune genes. The rhesus macaque MHC class I B region showed a compound evolutionary history indeed. Microsatellite analysis traced the tangled B loci quite fully. The new map aids primate disease models greatly.
plos-pone-0358987: Tourists don’t just visit heritage sites — they want to feel something real. This paper studied how ritualized experiences shape tourists’ sense of authenticity, and whether that feeling makes them willing to support preserving intangible cultural heritage. The findings tell heritage managers what turns a visit into a commitment.
plos-pone-0354687: Only a quarter of placental growth-restriction cases trigger preeclampsia — why? Mining a 24-year cohort of 90,000 births with 2,060 cases, this paper hunted the clinical risk factors that tip growth restriction into preeclampsia. The risk factors give obstetricians a sharper watch list.
plos-pone-0357287: GPs and public health teams need live virus intelligence, not last month’s reports. This paper described respiratory virology dashboards built for primary care and public health insight in England. The dashboards turn lab data into decisions — showing where flu and its viral cousins are surging, in near real time.
plos-pone-0357987: Systemic sclerosis hardens skin and organs — and pulmonary hypertension makes it far deadlier. This paper studied endothelial and platelet dysfunction in these patients. The vascular findings pinpoint where the disease damages blood vessels most, suggesting where treatments should aim.
plos-pone-0345687: An unknown seamount in the southeast Pacific hides completely unmapped life. This paper gave automated, quantitative characterization of its benthic habitat and associated biological communities. The baseline survey documents a pristine deep-sea ecosystem — before anyone has a chance to disturb it.
plos-pone-0357387: Manufacturing recombinant proteins and peptides is expensive, slow, and fiddly. This paper streamlined production using a pre-configured elastin-like polypeptide expression cassette. The ready-made cassette cuts the hassle from protein manufacturing, making custom proteins cheaper and faster to produce.
plos-pone-0357787: Cute, human-like chatbots make shoppers buy on impulse. This paper examined the mechanism of AI chatbot anthropomorphism on consumer impulse buying in live streaming scenarios, using the stimulus-organism-response framework. The findings show precisely how human-like bots pry open wallets during live sales.
plos-pone-0357487: Migrant women without medical insurance struggle to access perinatal care — with risks for mother and baby. This scoping review mapped interventions that facilitate their access to care. The synthesis points to the approaches that actually open doors, from community health workers to policy fixes.
plos-pone-0356687: Vegan honey tweaked in the laboratory can fight a notoriously drug-resistant bacterium. This paper showed that modifications to a vegan artificial honey produce inhibitory activity against Mycobacterium abscessus. The sweet result hints at a future of edible, honey-based antimicrobials for hard-to-treat infections.
plos-pone-0356887: Studying microbiomes at true scale demands serious throughput. This paper integrated uniform droplet-templated emulsification with FACS cell sorting for accessible, robust ultrahigh-throughput microbiome analysis. The combination lets researchers sort and sequence microbes by the millions — cheaply and reproducibly.
plos-pone-0356387: Semen may carry prostate cancer signals that go far beyond fertility testing. This paper uncovered the diagnostic potential of seminal fluid: cfDNA methylation analysis for detecting clinically significant prostate cancer. The fluid biopsy approach could transform screening into something far less invasive than current methods.
plos-pone-0357887: Social workers stand on the front lines against violent extremism — often unrecognized. This scoping review protocol will systematically map social work’s role in preventing and countering violent extremism. The planned review charts an emerging practice area that desperately needs an evidence base.
plos-pone-0356187: Parks, trails, and green corridors shape how we feel as we move through them. This paper mapped emotional patterns in linear recreational landscapes — their spatial structure, how positive and negative feelings co-occur, and the nonlinear drivers behind them. The emotional maps reveal exactly where green corridors lift moods and where they fall flat.
plos-pone-0348387: Morning people and night owls walk differently when their minds are busy. This study linked chronotype to dual-task gait cost across distinct cognitive domains in healthy young adults. The findings connect our body clocks to the mechanics of movement in surprising detail.
plos-pone-0356787: Middle ear infections — otitis media — remain a leading global cause of hearing loss. This paper mapped global patterns and demographic drivers of that hearing loss from 1990 to 2023. The three-decade trends guide prevention where the burden falls hardest.
plos-pone-0355187: Buried pipelines corrode invisibly until they fail catastrophically. This paper improved corrosion depth estimation using SMOTE-integrated machine and deep learning models. The enhanced models predict where pipes are thinning — so operators can intervene before the ground gives way.
plos-pone-0357087: Artificial reefs dot southern California’s coast — but which designs actually work? This paper produced high-resolution sonar mapping of the reefs, linking habitat metrics to construction material and design. The sonar-derived evidence tells reef builders what structures marine life genuinely prefers.
plos-pone-0356987: Rebuilding a 3D knee from flat X-rays and fluoroscopy could transform orthopedics. This systematic review surveyed methods and accuracy for two-dimensional to three-dimensional knee reconstruction from 1995 to 2025. The thirty-year synthesis shows how far the field has come — and what still limits it.
plos-pone-0355387: Cocoa farming is reshaping rural Colombia — for better and worse. This paper examined cocoa cultivation as an engine of rural development, tracing its impact on the livelihood strategies of rural households. The findings reveal how a single crop reconfigures entire rural economies.
plos-pone-0353787: University students face a mental health crisis — and exercise might help. This national prospective study examined physical exercise and the risk of common mental disorders among higher education students. The longitudinal findings strengthen the case for campus fitness as genuine mental health infrastructure, not just recreation.
plos-pone-0355687: Designing camping cookware with AI — while embedding sustainability from the start. This paper redefined the design innovation process through AI-generated camping cookware with sustainability baked in. The case study demonstrates how generative AI can serve ecological goals rather than merely accelerating consumption.
plos-pone-0356487: Tomatoes face drought with a family of response-regulator genes — the B-RRs. This paper identified the tomato B-RR gene family genome-wide and analyzed their expression under ABA hormone and drought stress. The genetic map points breeders toward tomatoes that sip water instead of guzzling it.
plos-pone-0354887: Basal cell carcinoma — the commonest skin cancer — involves cell-specific genes worth identifying. This paper leveraged expression quantitative trait loci at single-cell resolution to find them. The cell-specific gene list points to precise molecular targets in a cancer usually treated with a scalpel.
europmc-pmc2912887: Nonnegative matrix factorization splits data into meaningful parts, and this 2010 paper offers a flexible R package for it. The authors' NMF toolkit brought the method to R users everywhere. Their code spread a powerful math trick to working biologists who needed it.
europmc-pmc2944787: Orphan DNA islands mark hidden gene switches in mammals. This 2010 paper shows orphan CpG islands flag numerous conserved promoters in the mammalian genome. The authors' hunt reveals overlooked control regions. Their find expanded the genome's control map for researchers. Gene hunters still use the map today.
europmc-pmc2945087: Sepsis patients may get too little antibiotic too late. This 2010 paper finds insufficient beta-lactam levels in the early phase of severe sepsis and septic shock. The authors' measurements warn of underdosing. Their work pushed weight-based dosing in ICUs.
europmc-pmc2946687: Acinetobacter baumannii resists nearly every drug, and this 2010 review confronts the threat. The authors cover multidrug resistant acinetobacter, its spread, and its care. Their overview maps a nightmare germ. The review guides last-resort treatment. ICUs worldwide consult it when outbreaks hit.
europmc-pmc3026687: Malaria eradication needs a research agenda. This 2011 paper lays out the science needed to wipe out malaria. The authors chart drugs, vaccines, and mosquito work. Their work shaped global efforts. The agenda still guides funders today. Eradication remains decades away, they admit.
europmc-pmc3068987: Review methods got a worked example. This 2011 paper demos framework synthesis on views about cancer-preventing pills. The authors' example teaches the method. Their work guided reviewers. Students copy the worked steps. The method fits messy qualitative data. Review teams adopted it for policy work.
europmc-pmc3078587: A cheap blood ratio predicts chemo outcomes. This 2011 paper shows the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio forecasts chemo results in advanced bowel cancer. The authors validate the penny marker. Their work aids cancer doctors. High ratios meant shorter survival. Clinics adopted it for its zero cost.
europmc-pmc6522487: Why do different animals host such different gut bacteria? Comparing microbiomes across vertebrate species, researchers found two forces pulling in different directions: what an animal eats shapes one layer of its gut community, while deep evolutionary history shapes another. The finding, built partly on wild rather than captive animals, clarifies how diet and ancestry each mold the microbiome.
europmc-pmc6557987: Exercise is among the cheapest medicines for the heart - but how exactly does it protect? This review traces the pathways: workouts improve blood-vessel function, tame inflammation, and help the body handle sugar and fat. Against obesity-driven heart disease and diabetes, the authors argue, regular movement remains one of the most powerful tools available.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-987: The nation's attic filed its spending plan in 2007 — GAO's report reviews the Archives' budget for guarding America's paper memory. The findings check the dollars behind the documents, from vaults to reading rooms. History's keeper, the report implies, deserves books as orderly as its shelves.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-1087: Gold-star lenders were cashing in on student loans in 2007 — GAO's report says killing the ‘exceptional performer' perk would save serious money. The findings show the bonus label paid lenders extra for doing their jobs. The report's math: end the gold stars, keep the billions.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-387: Missile defense bought speed at a steep price in 2007, and GAO's report says the acquisition strategy delivered hardware but less capability for more money. The findings grade the trade-off in detail. The report's verdict is wry: results, yes — at a cost that would make a banker blush.
openalex-w7204598387: Online learning is here to stay, but what makes a good virtual classroom? This study reflects on e-learning environments today, using published research to analyze what helps students learn at a distance. The authors take a qualitative look at the digital spaces where modern education happens. A thoughtful overview for teachers building courses for screens.
openalex-w7204480187: A swollen gallbladder can rot, and surgeons now often take it out through small cuts even in bad cases. This paper sums up what studies say about keyhole gallbladder removal for severe sudden inflammation. The authors weigh safety and results. A surgery review tracking how far the small-cut method has come.
pmc-13452087: A 2026 methods paper on profiling protein-peptide interactions using yeast surface display, a technique that presents thousands of protein variants on yeast cells for high-throughput screening. Mapping which peptides bind which proteins is foundational for drug discovery. The protocol offers a practical route to large-scale interaction maps.
pmc-13450687: A 2026 multi-country Asian cohort study examining secondary prevention of heart attacks — the drugs and care given after a first MI — in people with dementia. Dementia patients often get less aggressive cardiac care, and the study measures the pattern across jurisdictions. The findings raise questions about equity in post-heart-attack treatment.
pmc-13456787: This 2026 clinical paper builds a risk-analysis and early-warning model for acute kidney injury after non-cardiac surgery. Kidney damage is a common, dangerous post-surgical complication, and the retrospective model flags at-risk patients from routine data. A reliable warning could let teams intervene before the kidneys fail.
pmc-13430587: This 2026 anthropology methods paper tackles a practical problem: estimating missing landmarks on fossil long bones using reverse engineering. Hominin fossils are often incomplete, and the authors lay out the challenges and potential solutions. Better estimation means more reliable conclusions about our ancestors' bodies.
pmc-13425587: In this 2026 sports science paper, researchers tested the validity and sensitivity of an extended field-of-view wireless palm-sized ultrasound device for measuring muscle hypertrophy. A pocket-sized scanner that accurately tracks muscle growth could change rehab and training. The study puts the gadget through its paces.
pmc-13493187: A 2026 drug development paper on building structure-activity relationships to avoid toxicity from unwanted ion channel activity in the central nervous system. Many drug candidates fail because they hit brain ion channels; designing that risk out early saves years. The paper shows how the team did it.
pmc-13450387: In this 2026 vision paper, photoswitchable small molecules — compounds that change shape with light — restored saccadic eye movements and visually guided behavior in ambient white light in an animal model. Light-activated molecules standing in for lost photoreceptors is a bold blindness therapy. The behavioral recovery is the headline.
pmc-13348487: In this 2026 autism paper, researchers found transcriptomic convergence — different genetic paths leading to similar gene-activity patterns — across synaptic, immune-glial, and RNA-regulatory axes in the human cerebral cortex. The convergence suggests shared biology beneath autism's heterogeneity. The cortical data are the study's strength.
pmc-13500787: This 2026 review expands perspectives on specialized metabolism in Streptomyces bacteria — the soil microbes that gave us most antibiotics. Their chemical repertoire is far from exhausted. The paper argues for fresh looks at old organisms.
pmc-13482287: A 2026 paper showing that blocking the CRH receptor 1 with an oral drug reduces endometriosis pain and associated adhesions. Stress-hormone signaling turns out to drive endometriosis pathology. The oral drug is a promising non-hormonal treatment.
pmc-13424687: A 2026 study testing how well cardiovascular risk prediction tools perform in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. Standard calculators may misfire in COPD patients. The performance check is a needed validation.
pmc-13633287: A 2026 review of mangrove sediments as carbon sinks — global research patterns, trends, and future directions. Mangroves bury carbon. The review maps the science.
pmc-13536887: In this 2026 chemistry paper, transition-metal ions influenced the photoisomerization of a pentadentate azopyridine ligand — the interplay of charge-transfer and metal-centered states. The light-driven switching was tuned by metals. The mechanism is the study.
pmc-13509387: In this 2026 paper, GCE — a framework for interpretable nonlinear hazard modeling — was applied to cardiac sarcoma survival using SEER data. The rare cancer's prognosis was modeled transparently. The framework is the advance.
pmc-13489787: In this 2026 catalysis paper, oxidation state influenced iron catalysts' activity for CO2 fixation to cyclic carbonates. The iron's charge tuned the chemistry. The influence is the design rule.
pmc-13470487: In this 2026 case report, rapidly destructive osteoarthritis of the hip followed multiple high-dose intra-articular steroid injections. The injections may have accelerated the destruction. The case is the caution.
pmc-13430087: This 2026 nephrology paper found persistent haematuria associated with reduced kidney survival in primary podocytopathies. The blood in urine predicted worse outcomes. The association is the prognostic marker.
pmc-13481687: In this 2026 scoping review, the Indian Medical Association's role in federal and state policy processes in India was examined. The medical lobby's influence was mapped. The review is the policy analysis.
pmc-13474987: This 2026 randomized controlled trial tested high-intensity interval training's effect on cardiorespiratory fitness for non-ambulatory stroke survivors. The HIIT worked for the wheelchair-bound. The trial is the rehabilitation evidence.
pmc-13472887: A 2026 study of mindfulness and psychological distress among Chinese taekwondo athletes — stress, self-management, and brooding as mediators. The athletes' minds were modeled. The mediating roles are the finding.
pmc-13485087: In this 2026 paper, cortical/cerebral visual impairment was addressed — from assessment to intervention. The brain-based vision loss's care pathway was laid out. The paper guides clinicians.
pmc-13424587: A 2026 paper: e-cigarette vaping was associated with pro-fibrotic gene expression in kidney and liver tissues. The vaping's organ fibrosis signal was found. The association is the warning.
pmc-13649487: A 2026 hepatology paper: "Beyond symptom relief" — the promise of linerixibat as a mechanism-based therapy for cholestatic pruritus in primary biliary cholangitis. The itch drug's mechanism was the hope. The promise is the therapeutic outlook.
pmc-13527087: A 2026 neuromorphic paper: broadband encoding and high-speed probabilistic bit generation with integrated microwave neurons. The microwave neurons computed. The bit generation is the hardware advance.
pmc-13439287: This 2026 cytology paper presented touch imprint cytology as a practical step toward standardized rapid on-site evaluation. The bedside cytology was standardized. The step serves pathology.
pmc-13417487: A 2026 paper: "Patient-Centered Teledermatology" — bridging pharmacies and dermatologists. The pharmacy-dermatology link was built. The bridging is the care model.
arxiv-2606-15987: Ancient manuscripts written in Sahidic Coptic — the main dialect of late ancient Egypt — are hard for computers to read. This paper releases a labeled dataset of these texts so researchers can train models to recognize the old handwriting. It is a building block for digitizing and preserving Egypt's early Christian-era written heritage.
arxiv-2606-16087: A graph theory paper on strong connectivity — when every point in a network can reach every other — and strong biconnectivity, a tougher version that survives the loss of any single connection. The author works through problems related to these properties, which matter for designing resilient communication networks. It targets specialists in graph algorithms.
arxiv-2606-16187: "Oblivious" programs hide not just your data but your access patterns — what you looked at and when — from anyone watching. obliv-clang brings this strong privacy property to real-world C++ programming as a practical compiler toolchain. The paper targets security engineers who need cryptographic privacy guarantees in software people actually run.
arxiv-2606-16487: Most statistics assumes well-behaved data, but real risks — market crashes, floods — come from heavy tails. This probability paper studies logarithmic large deviations for sums of heavy-tailed variables: how rare, extreme totals behave. It targets probabilists and risk modelers working where the normal distribution fails.
arxiv-2606-16587: Spray nozzles — in engines, printers, farm equipment — break liquid sheets into droplets, and simulating that breakup is brutally expensive. This paper learns a geometry-conditioned latent surrogate: a fast AI stand-in that predicts spray formation from the nozzle's shape. It targets engineers who need spray simulations without supercomputer bills.
arxiv-2606-16787: Gas giant exoplanets have wild atmospheres where tiny clusters of metal oxides may form — seeds of clouds. This paper studies those clusters: how they form and what they do in hot Jupiter-like skies. It is for astronomers modeling alien atmospheres.
arxiv-2606-16887: Tiny drums where light and jiggle wed are called optomechanical cavities. This paper weds two bending drums with built jiggle links, so the pair hums as one. It is for optomechanics pros who link light and motion. Linked drums sing together.
